newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone, Merck in joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Rhone, Merck in joint venture.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc SA and Merck & Co Inc announced on Thursday that they planned to merge their animal health and poultry engineering activities to create a joint venture company which they said would become the world leader in the sector.
Rhone and Merck will each hold 50 percent of the new company, to be called Merial.
The company will have estimated annual turnover of some 8.5 billion francs ($1.6 billion), a Rhone statement said. ($ = 5.26 French Francs)

The agreement to form the joint company was set out in a letter of intent signed on Thursday. Dependent on regulatory approval, Merial is expected to be fully operational in the second quarter of 1997.

Rhone, which described itself as the seventh largest pharmaceutical and chemicals group worldwide, said it and Merck, a major U.S. pharmaceutical products and services firm, had achieved "considerable success" in the animal health and poultry genetics market through their companies Rhone Merieux and Merck AgVet.

In 1995, Rhone Merieux's and Merck's animal health businesses held fourth and second-place market rankings respectively. Their combined 1996 sales will be seven billion francs in a market totalling 53 billion francs.

"Merck and Rhone-Poulenc's animal health businesses are fully complementary, forming an excellent fit in terms of product line, pipeline and species and geographic representation," said Merck chairman Raymond Gilmartin.
